_comment: THE canonical version-matrix construct catalogue (VERSION_TEST_MATRIX_DESIGN.md §10 #5). Each entry: a minimal program exercising ONE construct + its edition metadata. VersionMatrixTests computes the expected outcome per (construct × edition): compiles iff introducedIn <= V and (removedIn null or V < removedIn). The human-readable VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md and the in-code ConstructDialectStatus registry are renderings of THIS file — extend it here, never fork. 'vcr' cites the VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row/section or the introducing standard where the doc has no row (it covers 2002→2023 deltas only). OPTIONAL 'status': 'pending' = catalogued (edition metadata frozen by the drift tests) but not yet implemented — the matrix SKIPS its compile assertions until the owning roadmap phase lands and flips it active (the one pending mechanism, shared with the corpus discovery manifests). Vendor-dialect constructs live in vendor-constructs.json (owner decision 2), never here.

constructs.description: INVOKE (OO method call), ISO §14.9.23 — introduced 2002. The row is kept because the extension is accepted (the shipped 2002/goback_returning.cob golden runs it) and is gated at 2002 because GOBACK itself is a 2002 introduction — but it no longer cites a GOBACK clause as the authority for a phrase that clause does not contain.

constructs.description: The USAGE clause's per-item endianness-phrase and encoding-phrase (ISO §13.18.60.2 general format: FLOAT-BINARY-32/-64/-128 [ endianness-phrase ], and FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/-34 with a bracketed choice-indicator group over { encoding-phrase, endianness-phrase }) — a COBOL-2014 addition arriving with the standard floating-point usages themselves. §13.18.60.4 GR19a/b give the phrase its meaning (HIGH-ORDER-LEFT = big-endian, HIGH-ORDER-RIGHT = little-endian) and GR19c/d make the OPTIONS FLOAT-BINARY / FLOAT-DECIMAL clause supply the IMPLIED phrase only where the item states none — so the item's own phrase WINS, per §11.9.8.3 SR2/SR3's 'in which an endianness-phrase is not specified'. Recognition-based on the parsed floatFormatPhrase, like the noSignPhrase row above: the phrase is a modifier, not a usage keyword, so it cannot be keyed on the resolved Usage enum. Annex A.3 item 18 makes the phrase processor-dependent AND requires that when the FLOAT-BINARY clause is supported, the USAGE-clause phrases match it — WiseOwl COBOL supports both phrases in both places.

constructs.description: The BYTES spelling of the RECORD clause's { BYTES | CHARACTERS } brace group (ISO 13.18.43.2, all three general formats; 13.18.43.3 SR2 "The words BYTES and CHARACTERS are synonymous and may be used interchangeably") - a COBOL-2023 addition. Annex E.3.3 item 13 lists BYTES among the words added to the context-sensitive-word list at 2023, and 8.10 gives BYTES exactly ONE construct, the RECORD clause, so item 13's alternative "or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" cannot be what it names here: the spelling did not exist below 2023. CHARACTERS is 1985-continuous and stays ungated; only the BYTES word is gated - the CONTINUE AFTER ... SECONDS precedent, from the same item-13 family. BYTES also stays a nameSlot user word at every edition (cobol-words.json), so `01 BYTES PIC X.` is legal COBOL-85 source: the gate is on the CLAUSE, never on the word. kb/Work PB721.

directivePlacement.text: The LEAP-SECOND directive shall not be specified within a compilation unit

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §7.3.17.2 general format: LEAP-SECOND and OFF are underlined, ON is not, so per §5.2.3 a bare >>LEAP-SECOND selects ON — the 'specified or implied' case §7.3.17.4 GR2/GR4 presuppose. The directive's PLACEMENT rule (§7.3.17.3 SR1, not within a compilation unit) stays with its stage as COBOLNET1650.

constructs.description: The >>LEAP-SECOND [ON|OFF] compiler directive (ISO §7.3.17) — a COBOL-2002 compiler-directive introduction (§7.3): with ON in effect a formatted-time argument's seconds subfield may be 60 (§15.3.3.3) and a standard numeric time form value is bounded at 86,401 (§7.3.17.4 GR4) instead of 86,400 (GR5); the reported side (a 60 in the seconds position of the clock functions, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT >= 86,400) is implementor-defined and answered never (A.1 item 112). A text-manipulation-stage directive consumed by LeapSecondDirectiveProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive below 2002 (kb/Work PB65).

constructs.description: The >>FLAG-02 { ALL | option... } { ON | OFF } migration-flagging directive (ISO §7.3.14) — introduced in COBOL-2014 to flag 2002-to-2014 incompatibilities (GR1; the directive references the 2014 edition, and Annex E.2 item 5 lists only FLAG-14 as new to 2023, so FLAG-02 predates 2023). It is OBSOLETE (NOT removed) in COBOL-2023 — §7.3.14.1 NOTE: 'an obsolete element in this Working Draft International Standard and is to be deleted from the next edition'. Per §4.2.13 an implementation SHALL SUPPORT obsolete elements, so at 2023 it STILL COMPILES and carries the COBOLNET0903 obsolete warning (never a 0902 removal error). Modeled introducedIn=2014 + obsoleteIn=2023: the introduction gate rejects below 2014, the obsolete gate warns at 2023.
constructs.citation: ISO §7.3.14; §7.3.14.1 NOTE (obsolete in 2023); §4.2.13 (obsolete elements shall be supported + warned)

It modifies which words are reserved / context-sensitive / intrinsic-function words and prohibits specified user-defined words, per compilation group, during the text-manipulation stage. Recognized and parsed by CobolWordsDirectiveProcessor into a CobolWordsMap consumed by the post-lex token rewriter + the composed ReservedWordSet + intrinsic-name resolution; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2023.

constructs.description: The >>CALL-CONVENTION {COBOL | convention-name} compiler directive (ISO §7.3.9) - it associates a convention-name with a set of implementor-defined call conventions for CALL/INVOKE and the ENTRY convention. constructs.description: Compile-time arithmetic expression MODE (ISO §7.3.6.3 GR2) - a CONFIRMED BEHAVIOR VARIANT (INV-3; kb/Work PB1592). Annex E.2 item 6 makes the mode implementor-defined only at COBOL-2023 and records the prior rule ('The previous COBOL Standard required the use of an arithmetic mode that is no longer supported'); the one mode 2023 removed is Standard Arithmetic (E.2 item 21). So at 2002/2014 a compile-time arithmetic expression (CONSTANT AS, >>DEFINE, >>IF/>>EVALUATE) evaluates in standard arithmetic - the SDIDI decimal engine, 34 digits, NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO - and at 2023 in the documented System.Decimal mode (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-29). The edge is the runtime behaviour register's DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined, read by CompileTimeArithmetic.For; this row carries the per-edition OUTPUT witness. The source's constant 0.0000000000000000000000000015 / 2 * 10000000000000000000000000000 is 7.5E-28 exactly in the SDIDI (x1E28 = 7.5, GR3 -> 7) and a tie rounded to the even 8E-28 in System.Decimal (-> 8). The construct itself (a compile-time arithmetic expression) is a COBOL-2002 introduction with the constant entry and the >> directives, so COBOL-85 refuses the source with the constant entry's introduction gate (COBOLNET0900).

constructs.description: The multiple LINE clause (§13.18.35.3 SR10) — more than one operand defines a set of report lines at possibly-unequal vertical intervals. LIVE (kb/Work PB565): §13.18.35.4 GR9 makes it "functionally equivalent to a LINE clause with a single operand, together with a simple OCCURS clause whose integer is equal to the number of operands of the LINE clause", so the binder builds exactly that — a simple, STEP-less, VERTICAL repeating entry whose per-repetition operand the LINE clause supplies — and it drives the same subtree replay as §13.18.38 format 3. SR10 a/b/c/d are enforced on COBOLNET2199. The COBOL-85 LINE clause was the single-operand LINE NUMBER IS, so the multi-operand form AND the LINES / NUMBERS / ARE spellings of §13.18.35.2 Format 1 (kb/Work PB1221: the keyword prefix is the closed brace LINE NUMBER IS | LINE NUMBERS ARE | LINES ARE) are introduction-gated (0900 below 2002).

constructs.description: The OCCURS clause in a report group description entry (§13.18.38 format 3 — OCCURS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 TIMES [DEPENDING ON data-name-1] [STEP integer-3]): a REPEATING ENTRY, which §13.18.38.4 GR10 makes "define integer-2 distinct report items", GR11 gives every repetition the same PICTURE/VALUE/JUSTIFIED/BLANK WHEN ZERO/GROUP INDICATE effect, GR12 spaces by the STEP phrase and GR13 counts by the DEPENDING operand. LIVE ON BOTH AXES (kb/Work PB565): the binder REPLAYS the entry's subtree once per repetition, so §13.18.63.4 GR21's import of GR9 (a VALUE reaches every occurrence) and GR22's OCCURS-DEPENDING suppressor both ride it. The entry's AXIS is fixed by the clause it carries — a LINE clause on the entry or in its subtree repeats it VERTICALLY (GR10c/GR10d, GR12c/GR12d), anything else horizontally (GR10a/GR10b, GR12a/GR12b) — and integer-3 displaces on that axis only. The COBOL-85 report group description entry had no OCCURS clause at all.
constructs.display: OCCURS (report group description — a repeating entry)

constructs.description: The UNDERSCORE as a character of a COBOL word (a user-defined word here) — ISO §8.3.2.1: "Each character of a COBOL word … shall be selected from the set of basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore. The hyphen or underscore shall not appear as the first or last character in such words." A COBOL-2002 introduction: the '85 word character set has the hyphen only. Parsed at EVERY edition (superset-parse / bind-narrow) so the below-2002 rejection is this named gate rather than a raw `no viable alternative`. fix-queue R02.

constructs.description: A COBOL word whose characters the COBOL 2002/2014 Annex B permits where they stand and the COBOL 2023 Annex B does not — Annex E.2 item 4: U+037A GREEK YPOGEGRAMMENI was deleted, and U+30FB KATAKANA MIDDLE DOT may no longer be a word's first or last character (B.3 item 3, medial only). Modeled as removedIn=2023: compiles at 2002/2014, rejected at 2023 (COBOLNET0902; --permissive downgrades to a warning and keeps the 2014 rule). Every other Annex B violation is COBOLNET2773 at every edition. kb/Work PB1402.

constructs.description: A program or function source unit WITHOUT the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header — ISO §11.2.1 prints `[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]` in brackets (rendered, PDF p293 / folio 263), so the unit may open directly on its PROGRAM-ID or FUNCTION-ID paragraph. X3.23-1985 required the header, so the header-less form is a 2002 relaxation. Parsed at every edition (superset-parse) so the below-2002 rejection is this named gate rather than `unexpected 'PROGRAM-ID'`. kb/Work PB829.

constructs.description: OBJECT-COMPUTER clauses WITHOUT computer-name-1 — ISO §12.3.6.2 makes computer-name-1 optional and lets the clauses (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION) follow the paragraph's period directly. X3.23-1985 hung the clauses (MEMORY SIZE, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SEGMENT-LIMIT) off a REQUIRED computer-name, so the name-less clause form is a 2002 relaxation; the empty paragraph (and SOURCE-COMPUTER's, §12.3.5.2) was legal at 85 already. Parsed at every edition (superset-parse / bind-narrow) so the below-2002 rejection is this named gate rather than `unexpected 'PROGRAM'`. kb/Work PB78.

constructs.description: SET CONTENT OF { identifier-14 } … TO { FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO [IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE] | FLOAT-INFINITY | FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER | FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING | NEAREST-TO-ZERO [IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE] } [SIGN {NEGATIVE|POSITIVE}] (ISO §14.9.39.2 Format 15, numeric-content) — set a numeric item to an extreme its own description permits (GR32/GR36) or a standard floating-point item to an ISO/IEC 60559:2020 canonical infinity / quiet NaN / signaling NaN (GR33/GR34/GR35). MANDATORY base language: neither Annex A.3 nor Annex A.4 carries it (A.4's whole SET inventory is formats 6, 11/12 and 14). Recognition gate on setContentStatement — syntactically self-identifying, so it fires in the ParseArm. kb/Work PB452.
